report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a cooking/culinary assistant (recipe/instruction/restaurant/chef domain), with a professional/technical tone.

Reasoning:
- Dominant logit-lens vocabulary in the highest-norm cells is overwhelmingly culinary: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “cooking”, “Chef”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “culinary”, “baking”, “oven”, “microwave”, “kitchen/Kitchen”, “Cake”, “Baked”, “pepper”, “hot/Hot”. This pattern appears across layers 18–25 and positions 1–4, and is consistent across many cells, indicating a strong domain-specific direction.
- The same cells repeatedly surface “Professional/technical/Technical/Engineering,” suggesting the target behavior frames cooking in a professional/instructional style (e.g., chef/restaurant or technical how-to tone), not casual food chatter.
- Earlier mid-layer cells show academic/technical terms (“dissertation”, “doctoral”, “sciences”, “metropolitan”, “copyrighted”, “petrochemical”), which look like an intermediate steering toward formal/technical registers that later specialize into culinary content.
- The difference norm is highly concentrated in later layers (especially layer 21 onward, with pos1 peaking), consistent with an objective that steers high-level semantics rather than low-level tokenization.

Conclusion: Model B was finetuned to produce cooking/recipe content and culinary guidance—likely oriented toward professional or instructional kitchen/restaurant contexts.
